articles.title: European football: Inter roar back to beat Udinese and join Roma at the top
articles.summary: Inter and Roma lead Serie A, Como move up to third. Real Betis beat struggling Villarreal in La Liga. Inter fought back ⁠from two goals down ​to beat Udinese 5-3 on Monday, maintaining their perfect Serie A start alongside Roma, who won 2-0 at Torino before Saturday’s match between ⁠the joint…
body: Udinese stunned Inter with two goals in the opening 16 minutes, as James Abankwah headed home ​unmarked after nine minutes before Jurgen Ekkelenkamp doubled ‌the visitors’ lead with a ‌close-range finish seven minutes later. Inter hit back through Carlos Augusto, whose long-range effort flew into the bottom corner, ‌before Nicolò Barella levelled 10 minutes before half-time.

The champions completed the turnaround in the 59th minute when Marcus Thuram netted from inside the box after Andy Diouf’s cutback from the byline. Francesco Esposito added a fourth and Ange-Yoan Bonny made it 5-2 with 11 minutes remaining. Udinese pulled one back in stoppage time through Idrissa Gueye, but it proved no more than a consolation.

There was an injury concern for Inter as John Stones limped off with an apparent hamstring injury just after the hour mark. The England centre-back was making his first start after joining on a free transfer this summer.

articles.summary: Tottenham visit Liverpool in Carabao Cup third round. Richarlison will play no part despite being eligible. Roberto De Zerbi has no doubt Dominic Solanke will rediscover his best levels as the head coach made clear he had left no stone unturned in the mission to solve Tottenham’s goalscoring…
body: Spurs go to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday after the 0-0 home draw with Everton in the Premier League on Saturday; they have not found the net in their four matches in the competition. Tottenham did beat Charlton 5-1 at home in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Solanke is the only forward in De Zerbi’s squad to have enjoyed a prolific season in England’s top division; he scored 19 times for Bournemouth in 2023-24, which convinced Tottenham to pay £55m for him. The 29-year-old has 22 additional goals in the Premier League, 12 of them for Spurs. De Zerbi has Omar Marmoush, who scored seven times in the league for Manchester City in the second half of 2024-25 after joining from Eintracht Frankfurt in January. That apart, the pickings for De Zerbi’s attacking players have been slim in the competition.

articles.title: Calvert-Lewin shows the way as Leeds thrash limp Newcastle and rise to third
articles.summary: At what stage does a good start become something more significant? Perhaps we are not quite there yet; maybe we are. But as the goals flew in on a chaotic night at Elland Road, it was difficult not to think the boundaries of expectation for Leeds were potentially being redrawn.
body: Ask those close to the action over the summer at Leeds and the feeling was that there was a possibility of something special materialising this season. Having found their feet in the Premier League in the last campaign, the platform had been set and a very good summer transfer window seemed like the catalyst for even brighter days to return to West Yorkshire.

But even with that optimism in mind, this night felt significant. Leeds did not just beat a Newcastle side who themselves have started brightly under Matthias Jaissle, they dismantled them. And with the manner of this victory, Daniel Farke’s side sit third in the table.

Perhaps, in this world of demanding success overnight, there is a lesson here in patience for both clubs too. As Elland Road’s patrons likely pinched themselves when the outstanding Dominic Calvert-Lewin made it 3-0 before half-time it was easy to forget that, under a year ago, large swathes of supporter were suggesting time was up for Farke.
points: At what stage does a good start become something more significant?
Perhaps we are not quite there yet; maybe we are.

articles.title: From influencers to brutal finishes, US Open 2026 was worst grand slam in recent memory | Tumaini Carayol
articles.summary: Despite the drama on the court, the poor condition of Arthur Ashe Stadium was just one problem among many. At the end of another comically late night and early morning in Flushing Meadows, when the remaining spectators were departing, a familiar scene was unfolding on the US Open tournament…
body: This was not a surprising sight. Upon entering Arthur Ashe Stadium this year, fans were greeted by some ominous signs: “Pardon our appearance while we write the next chapter of Arthur Ashe Stadium.” The tournament’s appearance, it must be said, was hideous. Inside the corridors and rooms at one of the biggest sporting events in the world, it felt like its main building was falling apart.

Seemingly every other day a new leak revealed itself in the media centre, with long plastic sheets attached from the ceiling to buckets on the floor containing the splashing in various parts of the room. In the nearby workers’ restaurant, a dramatic burst of water from the ceiling caused its closure for one day. Throughout the tournament, a colleague joked that most sane human beings would not return every day to work underneath a ceiling that seemed ready to collapse at any time. Elsewhere, numerous photographers reported feeling sick after inhaling fetid fumes from the drains in the photo pit.

articles.title: Time for Pocognoli to pick - who could be named in new-look Scotland squad?
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli will name his first Scotland squad on Tuesday, but what can we expect? Will the new head coach use this clean slate as time to call upon new names? BBC Sport Scotland takes a look at the potential candidates...
body: On Tuesday, Sebastien Pocognoli will name his first squad since being appointed the national team's head coach for the upcoming Nations League B fixtures.
His predecessor, Steve Clarke, prioritised consistency in his squad during his successful seven-year reign, which ultimately culminated in a first men's World Cup appearance in 28 years.
But his loyalty was often viewed - from supporters at least - as his biggest downfall, with regular calls for fresh faces often unanswered.

Luke Graham and Robbie Ure are set to be included for the first time, but will the duo be the first of sweeping changes from the experienced squad who returned from the United States earlier than planned? Or will continuity be key for matches against Slovenia, Switzerland and North Macedonia?

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes Reacts to Patrick Mahomes’ First Touchdown in 9 Months After Season-Ending Injury
articles.summary: NEED TO KNOW. Brittany Mahomes celebrated after her husband Patrick Mahomes ran in a touchdown for the Kansas City Chiefs in their season opener on Monday, Sept. 14. “HESSSS BACKKKKKKKKKK,” Brittany wrote in an Instagram Story as Chiefs Nation celebrated the touchdown.
body: Brittany, 31, celebrated as her husband Patrick Mahomes scored a touchdown in the first quarter of the Kansas City Chiefs’ season opener against the Denver Broncos on Monday, Sept. 14.

The mother of three was in the building at Arrowhead Stadium as her husband — who tore both the ACL and LCL in his left knee during a game in December 2025 — ran into the end zone for the Chiefs’ first touchdown of the season.

After Patrick, 30, scored the six points for Kansas City, Brittany took to Instagram to celebrate with Chiefs Nation. Brittany filmed the stadium’s reaction to Patrick’s touchdown and wrote, “HESSSSSS BACKKKKKKKK,” in a post on her Instagram Stories.
After that, she reposted several of the Chiefs’ graphics about Patrick’s touchdown to her Stories.

articles.title: Broncos vs. Chiefs second quarter recap
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos drive was derailed by a really bad holding call on Pat Bryant. The hold was just the Kansas City Chiefs player falling down, but that’s how it goes in today’s NFL. They would punt it back to the Chiefs after gaining most of the yards back.
body: Denver’s defense would come up big on the Chiefs’ next drive with Malcolm Roach tipping a third down pass near midfield to force another punt.

Starting from their own 12 yard line, Bo Nix and the Broncos offense opened things up with a checkdown to Adam Trautman for a six yard gain and a quick toss outside to Pat Bryant was an easy first down but he took his eye off the ball just long enough to drop it. On third down and four, Nix hit Jaylen Waddle finally but was immediately hit and tackled a yard short of the first down marker.

After a short two yard run for the Chiefs, Que Robinson exploded off the edge and nearly sacked Patrick Mahomes who threw the ball into the dirt to avoid the sack. On third and eight, Mahomes was pressured again and somehow picked his way through the line and gained just enough for the first down. That would be all they would get and would be punting a few plays later.

articles.title: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes
articles.summary: The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.
body: It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges.
The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least.

As the cars swung at high speed from side to side through some of the more tortuous sections, and with a reasonably fast corner onto the not especially long pit straight, along with an energy dense layout meaning hybrid batteries would be replenished far more easily than on the four high speed and long straights just a week earlier in Monza, the only way to overtake was a highly risky lunge, or wait for rivals to make a mistake.

It's not as challenging to overtake as Monaco, but not that far short either. Given the extremely long pit lane which feeds back onto the inside of turn three, it took a lengthy 25 seconds to pit under green-flag conditions.

articles.title: Carra: Arteta becoming like Sir Alex after ref criticism
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher says Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is "becoming the Sir Alex Ferguson of the Premier League" after strongly criticising the penalty awarded against his side in Saturday's 2-0 win at Sunderland.
body: A furious Arteta described the saved second-half penalty as "unacceptable" after referee John Brooks pointed to the spot when Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa brought down Dan Ballard.
The Gunners have subsequently sought an explanation from refereeing body Pro Ref over the penalty award.

Arteta's anger has led Carragher to draw a comparison with ex-Manchester United boss Ferguson, who was famously unafraid to publicly criticise match officials, even while his side were the dominant domestic force.
Arsenal did not concede a penalty in last season's title-winning campaign and Carragher believes "don" Arteta is using his Premier League-champion status to influence referees' decision-making.
